teachbacks.text:
1. Customer presses Place order. Cart sets its status to AWAITING_PAYMENT (read-only). It reuses the open attempt id or creates one, stores it with the cart, and sends the cart snapshot plus attempt id to Order over HTTP. If no reply comes, Cart retries with the same attempt id, and the retry returns the order's current status.
2. Order creates a record with status PENDING_STOCK, holding the frozen lines and prices. The record is unique on the attempt id, so a repeated press or retry returns the same order.
3. Order asks Inventory over HTTP to reserve all lines, keyed by the order id. Inventory first looks for a reservation row for that order id. If one exists it returns it and reserves nothing new. Otherwise it checks every line in one transaction.
4. Failure at this step, short stock. Nothing is reserved and nothing is charged. Order sets REJECTED_OUT_OF_STOCK and replies to Cart with the short items. Cart goes back to OPEN, shows the short items, and leaves the cart unchanged so the customer can edit and retry.
5. Failure at this step, Inventory silent. Order retries with the same key. If there is still no reply, Order sets CHECKOUT_FAILED and replies to Cart with a reason. Cart goes back to OPEN and shows the failure message. Order also asks Inventory to release, keyed by order id, and retries until Inventory acknowledges. A release for an order id with no row writes a RELEASED row, so a late reserve holds nothing. The sweeper is the backstop.
6. Success path. Inventory creates a reservation HELD for the order id, holds the stock, and sets expires_at to created time plus 10 minutes. It replies "reserved" to Order.
7. Order asks Payment over HTTP to charge, keyed by order id. Payment records the charge as PENDING before it calls the provider, then replies PENDING to Order. Order retries the charge call with the same key until Payment answers, and does not give up while a charge may exist. Order then sets AWAITING_PAYMENT and replies AWAITING_PAYMENT to Cart. Cart shows "payment pending" with the order id and stays read-only.
8. Payment calls the provider's charge using the order id as the idempotency key. It retries with the same key on timeout or 5xx. The outcome arrives later, either by webhook (seconds to 30 minutes) or by a status query after 30 minutes with no outcome. Payment owns that 30-minute timer.
9. When a webhook arrives, Payment verifies the signature and reads the provider event id. If the id is already recorded, it acknowledges only: no state change and no event. If not, it looks at the outcome and the charge state.
10. If the charge is already final, the same outcome changes nothing. The opposite outcome is recorded as a conflict, ops are alerted, and no event is published.
11. Declined path. Payment, in one transaction, sets the charge to DECLINED, records the event id, and writes PaymentDeclined to its outbox. A relay publishes it to the broker. Order consumes it and sets PAYMENT_DECLINED. Order asks Inventory to release the stock, retrying with the same key, and publishes OrderFailed with reason DECLINED. Cart receives it, and if it is AWAITING_PAYMENT and the attempt id matches, sets OPEN and shows a fixed message for that reason code. The cart is not emptied.
12. Succeeded path. Payment, in one transaction, sets the charge to SUCCEEDED, records the event id, and writes PaymentSucceeded to its outbox. The relay publishes it. Order consumes it and asks Inventory to claim, keyed by order id, retrying with the same key until it gets an answer.
13. Inventory's claim is one conditional update. It succeeds if the reservation is HELD and now is before expires_at, or if it is already CLAIMED for this order id, which makes retries safe. Otherwise it refuses. A RELEASED or EXPIRED reservation is refused, and an expired hold is refused even if the sweeper has not yet run.
14. Claim accepted. Order sets CONFIRMED and writes OrderConfirmed to its outbox, which is published. Cart applies it only if its status is AWAITING_PAYMENT and the attempt id matches. It then sets OPEN and empties the cart in the same step. A duplicate finds the status already OPEN and does nothing. An event for an older attempt is ignored.
15. Claim refused, the late-success case. The 10-minute hold can lapse before a webhook that may take up to 30 minutes, so this is a normal path. Order, in one transaction, sets CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK and refund state REQUESTED. A retry loop then sends the refund command to Payment, keyed by "refund:" plus order id, until Payment replies. If Order crashes in between, the stored state makes the loop resume after restart. A timeout on the claim is never treated as a refusal. Only an explicit refusal starts a refund.
16. Payment records the refund as PENDING and replies REFUND_PENDING to Order. It calls the provider to refund the full amount with the same key. On failure it keeps the refund open, retries with backoff, and alerts ops. The refund is never dropped, and Payment does not tell Order about the failure.
17. On refund success, Payment, in one transaction, sets the refund to SUCCEEDED and writes RefundSucceeded to its outbox. Order consumes it and sets CANCELLED_REFUNDED. It publishes OrderFailed with reason OUT_OF_STOCK and emails the customer. Cart applies it like any other OrderFailed (back to OPEN, out-of-stock message, cart unchanged).
18. Duplicates and ordering. The broker delivers at least once. A consumer acknowledges only after its state change and outbox rows are committed. The relay may publish twice. In Order, a message asking for the status the order already has is a no-op. A message whose move is not in the transition table is acknowledged, logged as an error, and changes nothing. After a crash following the claim, the broker redelivers PaymentSucceeded, the claim retry returns CLAIMED, and the order is confirmed.
19. Stock cleanup. If a hold is never claimed within 10 minutes, Inventory's sweeper turns HELD past expires_at into EXPIRED and the stock goes back on sale.
gaps: Timeouts are not set anywhere: Cart's wait for Place order, Order's wait on Inventory (how many retries before CHECKOUT_FAILED), charge retries and refund backoff. There is also no give-up rule for an unreachable Payment.
How the customer enters card details, and how the payment method reaches the charge call, is not decided.
How the customer's page learns the final outcome from Cart (polling or push) is not specified.

The document does not say how Cart's retry timing works, or how Cart learns the outcome if the OrderConfirmed or OrderFailed event arrives while it is not AWAITING_PAYMENT. It only says the event is ignored.
It is unclear whether the provider returns the refund result synchronously or by webhook.

It is unclear whether the provider's immediate reply to a charge can carry a final outcome. It is also unclear how often Payment re-queries if the charge is still PENDING after the 30-minute query, and whether the provider's status-query API exists.
What happens to the money when the provider reports the opposite outcome for an already-final charge is undecided.
The document does not say how the sweeper is scheduled, or what happens to Order's state if the hold expires before PaymentSucceeded arrives. It only says the claim is refused.
The mechanics of the outbox relay are not described: how often it runs, and how it knows what is unpublished.
The document does not say what the customer sees or what happens if the refund keeps failing. The email is only sent after refund success, and the timing of that email is an open question.
Whether the stock reserved is returned when Order handles a CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK is not stated beyond 'not held by this order'. Re-reserving for a late success is explicitly not done.
How Order retries the pending release or the refund loop at the process level (what triggers the loop, what a 'pending releases' store looks like) is not described beyond the fact that it exists.
The reply format and error codes for the 'reason' on CHECKOUT_FAILED are not listed. Only DECLINED and OUT_OF_STOCK are defined for events, and the fixed customer messages are not given.

The document does not state what Cart does if Place order returns REJECTED_OUT_OF_STOCK or CHECKOUT_FAILED regarding the attempt id. It only says the attempt id is replaced when the next Place order starts a new attempt, and does not say how Cart gets a 'final status' for those HTTP-only outcomes in a way that triggers a new attempt.

teachbacks.text:
1. Customer presses Place order in Cart. Cart sets its status to AWAITING_PAYMENT (read-only). It reuses the open attempt id, or creates a new one if the last order reached a final status, and stores it with the cart. Cart sends the cart snapshot and attempt id to Order over HTTP. State held: Cart (lines, status, attempt id, order id, last applied order status).

2. Order receives Place order. It creates an order in PENDING_STOCK with frozen lines and a price snapshot. The record is unique on attempt id. If an order for that attempt id already exists, Order does not start over. It resumes the unfinished steps and replies per the retry table.

3. Order sends an HTTP reserve to Inventory for all lines, keyed by order id. If there is no reply, Order retries with the same key, up to a reserve-attempt limit (the value is not set). Order stores the number of reserve attempts.

4. Inventory looks for a reservation row for that order id. If one exists, it returns that row's answer. HELD or CLAIMED means reserved. SHORT returns the stored short items. RELEASED or EXPIRED means not reserved. If no row exists, it checks every line in one transaction.

5a. Short stock: Inventory writes a SHORT row (it holds nothing) with the short items and replies with them. Order moves PENDING_STOCK to REJECTED_OUT_OF_STOCK, stores the short items, and replies REJECTED_OUT_OF_STOCK to Cart. Cart, which is AWAITING_PAYMENT with a matching attempt id, sets OPEN, leaves the lines unchanged, shows the short items, and records a final status. Nothing is charged.

5b. No reply after the attempt limit: Order moves to CHECKOUT_FAILED and replies with a reason code. It writes a pending-release row in the same transaction, and a worker retries the release with the same key. The release writes a RELEASED row if there is no reservation, so a late reserve holds nothing. Cart applies the reply, sets OPEN and shows the reason. The reason codes are not listed.

5c. All lines free: Inventory writes a HELD row that expires in 10 minutes and holds the stock. It replies "reserved".

6. Order commits the move to AWAITING_PAYMENT before it sends any charge. It then sends an HTTP charge to Payment, keyed by order id.

7. Payment records the charge as PENDING before it calls the provider. It replies PENDING to Order. Order records charge acknowledged = yes and replies AWAITING_PAYMENT with the order id to Cart. Cart stays read-only and shows payment pending. If the acknowledgement does not arrive before the request time runs out, Order replies IN_PROGRESS. Cart then retries Place order with the same attempt id. Order retries the charge with the same key until Payment answers and does not give up while a charge may exist.

8. Payment calls the provider with the order id as idempotency key. It retries with the same key on timeout or 5xx. The outcome arrives by webhook (seconds to 30 minutes). If nothing arrives after 30 minutes, Payment queries the provider's status. An immediate reply that is already final is handled like a webhook.

9. Webhook handling. Payment verifies the signature and reads the provider event id. If that id is already recorded, it acknowledges and changes nothing. Otherwise, if the charge is PENDING, it does one transaction: charge SUCCEEDED or DECLINED, event id recorded, and PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined written to its outbox. If the charge is already final, the same outcome changes nothing. The opposite outcome is recorded as a conflict, operations are alerted and no event is published. A relay reads unpublished outbox rows on a timer, publishes them to the broker and marks them published. It can publish twice, so consumers must handle repeats.

10a. Declined: Order receives PaymentDeclined. It moves AWAITING_PAYMENT to PAYMENT_DECLINED, writes a pending release (retried with the same key until Inventory acknowledges), and writes OrderFailed (reason DECLINED) to its outbox. Inventory sets a HELD reservation to RELEASED. Cart receives OrderFailed. If status is AWAITING_PAYMENT, the attempt id matches and the cart id matches, it sets OPEN, keeps the lines, and shows a fixed decline message that carries no provider details.

10b. Success: Order receives PaymentSucceeded and sends an HTTP claim to Inventory, keyed by order id. It retries with the same key on silence. Inventory claims only if the row is HELD and now is before expires_at, or it is already CLAIMED. If claimed, Order moves to CONFIRMED and writes OrderConfirmed to its outbox in the same transaction. Cart receives it, sets OPEN, empties the cart and keeps the attempt id.

10c. Late success (the hold lapsed, which the document says is common): Inventory refuses the claim. Order moves to CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK with refund REQUESTED in one transaction and sends no release. A worker sends the refund to Payment with key refund:+order id until Payment replies REFUND_PENDING. Order then sets ACKNOWLEDGED. Payment records the refund, calls the provider with the same key and retries until it succeeds. A failed refund stays open and operations are alerted. On success Payment publishes RefundSucceeded. Order moves to CANCELLED_REFUNDED, publishes OrderFailed (OUT_OF_STOCK) and emails the customer. Cart shows payment pending the whole time, then the out-of-stock message.

11. Sweeper: Inventory's sweeper changes HELD rows past expires_at to EXPIRED. This does not change the order's status.

12. Consumers acknowledge a broker message only after their commit. A repeat that asks for the status the order already has is a no-op. A move not in the table is acknowledged, logged as an error and ignored. A payment result for an order still in PENDING_STOCK is not acknowledged, so the broker redelivers it and operations are alerted.

13. Crash recovery: after a restart, Order's recovery worker repeats a PENDING_STOCK reserve, an unacknowledged charge, or a REQUESTED refund, each with its stored key. Outbox rows are published after a restart.

14. Retries after the outcome is known: a retried Place order returns the reply from the table by order state. FINAL covers CONFIRMED, PAYMENT_DECLINED and CANCELLED_REFUNDED. AWAITING_PAYMENT covers an acknowledged charge or CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK. The stored short items or reason are returned for the rejected and failed states.
gaps: Open question 6: no values for HTTP timeouts, Cart's retry interval, the request time before IN_PROGRESS, the reserve attempt limit, charge retries or refund backoff.
The reason codes for CHECKOUT_FAILED and the customer message texts are not listed (open question 13).
How the customer enters card details and how the payment method reaches the charge call is not decided (open question 4).
Whether the provider offers a status-query API is unknown, and so is how often to re-query a charge that is still PENDING (open question 5).
Whether the refund result comes synchronously or by webhook is unknown (open question 3).
What happens to the money on a conflicting provider outcome is undecided (open question 11).
How the customer's page learns the outcome (polling or push from Cart) is undecided (open question 8).
Relay and sweeper timer intervals are not set (open question 12).
The hold is 10 minutes and the webhook can take 30. Whether the hold is lengthened is undecided (open question 1).
Whether the provider honours idempotency keys, and the broker retention window, are assumed rather than guaranteed (open question 7).
Order sends the email, but how it knows the customer's address or contact details is not stated. The Order storage list has no such field.
Cart's behaviour if a retried Place order gets an IN_PROGRESS or no reply forever is not bounded. No upper limit or give-up path is stated.
The document does not say how Order's claim retry ends if Inventory never answers. Retry is 'until answered', but there is no limit.
How Order learns of Payment's webhook-driven transitions for a charge stuck PENDING with no provider status API is not specified.
The document does not say how the broker routes events to Cart or Order (topics, queues or subscriptions).
What happens when Payment is unreachable for the refund command and Order's worker keeps retrying is not stated beyond 'repeats until REFUND_PENDING'.
It is not stated how Cart finds the order for a Place order retry beyond the attempt id, or what happens if Cart itself crashes between setting AWAITING_PAYMENT and sending the request.
The document does not say how a pending release that Inventory never acknowledges is escalated, other than the sweeper backstop.

The junior's listed gaps are real holes in the document, so the explanation is not fully correct.; Customer email address: the document says Order emails the customer but does not say where Order gets the address. Added open question 14 and a note in the Order storage list.; Cart crash after AWAITING_PAYMENT but before the request is sent: the document did not say what Cart does on restart. Added the stated mechanism (Cart resends with its stored attempt id, and Order finds the order by attempt id) and open question 15 for the trigger.; Pending release that Inventory never acknowledges: escalation beyond the sweeper backstop is not stated. Added open question 16.; Claim retry with no limit: Order retries the claim until Inventory answers and the document sets no limit. Added to open question 17, and the order stays AWAITING_PAYMENT meanwhile.; Broker routing (topics, queues or subscriptions) is not specified. Added open question 18.; Cart waiting on IN_PROGRESS or no reply forever has no bound. Extended open question 6.; Refund command with Payment unreachable: Order keeps retrying with no stated limit. Extended open question 6.; Charge stuck PENDING with no provider status API: no transition is specified. Extended open question 5.; How the Place order retry finds the order: the document states Order's record is unique on attempt id, so the retry looks it up by attempt id. This is now stated explicitly in the Place order rule.
